basis: Control position (COLLECTION.md s1 control positions, decisions.md R1): in April 2008 'Insight Venture Partners, Bessemer Venture Partners, Georgian Partners, Goldman Sachs, and other investors bought a majority interest in Syncsort' (Wikipedia), the year its long-time chief executive and majority shareholder 'sold a large portion of his stake'; the firm's listed date is 2008-03-31. The firm with its co-investor group acquired control, so there is no venture round.

Control position (COLLECTION.md s1 control positions, decisions.md R1): Bessemer's first entry, in October 2017, was the acquisition of WiredScore by an investor group led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Fifth Wall (Venture Capital Journal, 2017-10-12, 'Bessemer and Fifth Wall-led investor group acquires WiredScore'; Forbes, 2017-10-10, 'Jared Kushner Sells Majority Stake In Real Estate Tech Firm WiredScore'); the Series A of October 2018, where the two are named as previous backers (FinTech Global), came after it. Same transaction and citation as the legal-entity row ws-holdco-pbc, already ruled out; only the two headlines could be read, the articles are behind registration walls.

Control position (COLLECTION.md s1 control positions, decisions.md R1): Metalogix 'was acquired in 2008 by Insight Venture Partners, a private equity firm' (New Ventures BC), with an outside chief executive installed, and the firm's own date for its investment is 2008-09-30, the same transaction; at the 2014 sale to Permira 'the current owners, Insight Venture Partners and Bessemer Venture Partners', were bought out (Washington Technology, 'Metalogix bought by another private equity firm'). The firm with its co-investor acquired the company, so there is no venture round.

Control position (COLLECTION.md s1 control positions, decisions.md R1, the exception R7 names): in the transaction of 2024-11-18 'Centerbridge and Bessemer are taking a combined 51% voting interest in the firm' (Accounting Today), and the firm's own partner page (bvp.com/team/brian-feinstein): 'Brian also led growth buyout investments in Litify, LiveAuctioneers (acq), Beyond, Current, and CRI', set apart from his 'early-stage investments' and 'growth investments'. The firm with its co-investor acquired control of Carr, Riggs & Ingram's advisory business, so there is no venture round.

Control position (COLLECTION.md s1 control positions, decisions.md R1): a buyout by the firm's own account. The firm's own partner page (bvp.com/team/brian-feinstein): 'Brian also led growth buyout investments in Litify, LiveAuctioneers (acq), Beyond, Current, and CRI', set apart from his 'early-stage investments' and 'growth investments'; its Forge launch post names LiveAuctioneers beside NetSmart and TeamViewer (both ruled out as buyouts) among its companies with 'a growth buyout investment structure'. The transaction is the $47.6M of November 2014, the first outside money in a company founded in 2002; EDGAR's company search returns no filer under the company's name, so no Form D records it as a financing. The releases read do not state the stake, so the ruling rests on the firm's own label.

Control position (COLLECTION.md s1 control positions, decisions.md R1): a buyout by the firm's own account. The firm's own partner page (bvp.com/team/brian-feinstein): 'Brian also led growth buyout investments in Litify, LiveAuctioneers (acq), Beyond, Current, and CRI', set apart from his 'early-stage investments' and 'growth investments'; of the five, Litify (a majority stake, February 2023) and CRI (a combined 51% voting interest, November 2024) are confirmed as control by their own announcements. The transaction is the $42.5M of September 2019, which TechCrunch and Crunchbase News called a Series A without stating the stake; EDGAR's company search returns no filer named Beyond Pricing, so no Form D records it as a financing. The ruling rests on the firm's own label.
